## Acceptable Use Policy

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/acceptable-use-policy
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > Acceptable Use Policy
- Last modified: 2026-05-06T12:11Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler's Acceptable Use Policy.

This Acceptable Use Policy ("Policy") outlines acceptable uses of Zscaler’s and its affiliates’ products, platforms, professional services, support services, consulting services, and any other services provided by or on behalf of Zscaler (collectively, "Offerings"), including any Outputs (as defined in the Product Output Disclaimer), deliverables, or recommendations generated in connection with such Offerings. In this Policy, "you" and "your" refer to the Customer as defined in the End User Subscription Agreement or the applicable agreement ("Agreement") between you and Zscaler. By accessing any Offerings, you agree to this Policy. This Policy is incorporated into, and subject to, the terms of your Agreement. We reserve the right to modify this Policy at any time.

###### 1. Conduct and Information Restrictions

You may not engage in any of the following:

**1.1.** Posting, transmitting, or storing content that is libelous, obscene, threatening, defamatory, or that infringes any intellectual property rights or violates any applicable law;

**1.2.** Reproducing, distributing, or creating derivative works from material obtained through the Offerings without required permissions from the rights holder;

**1.3.** Sending unsolicited bulk messages ("Spam"), or transmitting large volumes of duplicative, empty, or oversized messages that disrupt any service;

**1.4.** Harvesting email addresses, screen names, or other identifiers without prior consent, including through spidering or spyware;

**1.5.** Falsifying or removing message headers; or

**1.6.** Impersonating any person or entity, forging signatures, falsifying sender addresses, or engaging in phishing or similar fraudulent activity.

###### 2. Technical and Network Restrictions

**2.1.** You may not access any computer, system, network, software, or data without the owner's consent, or attempt to breach or circumvent the security of any host, network, or account. You may not use or distribute security-compromising tools such as password guessing programs, keystroke loggers, packet sniffers, or Trojan Horse programs. Unauthorized port scanning is strictly prohibited. You may not copy, distribute, sublicense, or make unauthorized modifications to any Zscaler Offerings.

**2.2.** You may not interfere with any entity's use of the Offerings, including by transmitting malicious code or generating disruptive traffic levels. You may not degrade the performance of the Offerings or any Zscaler infrastructure through denial of service attacks, network flooding, service overloading, or any similar means.

###### 3. Zscaler AI Features Use

**3.1.** This section governs your use of any Zscaler functionality powered by or incorporating artificial intelligence or machine learning (“AI Features”), including chatbots, policy recommendations, generative outputs, AI-assisted security assessments, AI red teaming tools (such as the SPLX platform). AI Features include AI-powered or AI-assisted capabilities whether embedded in Zscaler products, delivered through professional services, tech support, threat hunting, consulting, or otherwise made available by Zscaler personnel or contractors. Zscaler may introduce new or updated AI Features from time to time. Your use of such AI Features is automatically subject to this Policy upon its release, without the need for separate notice or consent.

**3.2.** AI Features rely on machine learning algorithms, large language models, and other advanced technology. They are not human, and their outputs may be incomplete, inaccurate, or inappropriate and should not be relied upon without independent verification. You are solely responsible for evaluating and verifying all AI-generated outputs before taking any action on them. See the [Product Output Disclaimer](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/product-output-disclaimer) for additional terms. For your privacy and security, do not share any personal or sensitive information.

**3.3.** When using AI Features you may not access, use, or enable others to access or use AI Features in any manner that would be in conflict with these rules:

**3.3.1.** Comply with applicable laws. Do not violate any applicable law including conduct that describes, supports, or distributes in any form child sexual abuse materials. Do not override safety or privacy filters, controls, or mechanisms.

**3.3.2.** Do not use AI Features to harm. Do not use AI Features to generate, facilitate, or distribute content that: (a) harms or threatens harm to any individual; (b) is sexually explicit or exploitative; (c) violates or infringes the rights of others; or (d) is intentionally or reasonably foreseeably misleading or deceptive. AI Features do not provide, and should not be treated as, medical, legal, financial, or any other kind of professional advisory services. If searching for important information, always verify the output with authoritative sources.

**3.3.3.** Do not misuse AI Features. Any attempts to exploit AI Features for malicious purposes like system interference, hacking or distributing malware are not allowed. Similarly, using AI Features for creating training data for other AI systems without Zscaler’s permission is not allowed. You may not reverse engineer, decompile, or attempt to extract the model weights, algorithms, or underlying architecture of any AI Features, or systematically probe AI Features to reconstruct their training data or decision logic.

**3.3.4**. Not designed nor intended for High Risk Activity. AI Features are not designed nor intended for any purpose requiring fail-safe performance, including stock trading, financial transaction processing, public transit systems, operation of nuclear facilities, electrical grid management, aircraft navigation or communication systems, air traffic control, life support machines, or weapons systems, or any other safety management or operation of critical infrastructure or hazardous applications for which failure could result in significant risk of death, personal injury, or severe physical, property, or environmental damage (each a “High Risk Activity”). Do not use any Offering or any of its AI Features as a safety component for any High Risk Activity.

**3.4.** AI Features’ Outputs are for general informational purposes only and should not be relied upon as the sole basis for any decision or action, including consequential decisions such as those impacting a person’s employment status, health, or safety. You are solely responsible for verifying Outputs before taking or refraining from taking any action.

**3.4.1.** Do not input sensitive information. Zscaler does not need or require sensitive personal information to provide AI Features. You and your users should not upload or input sensitive personal information into AI Features. Please ensure that your users abide by your internal data security and privacy policies. You are solely responsible for having appropriate internal policies regarding what types of information may and may not be submitted to AI Features. Zscaler shall not be liable for any loss, disclosure, or misuse of sensitive or confidential information that you or your users submit to AI Features in violation of your own policies or applicable law.

###### 4. Right to Monitor and Terminate Access

**4.1.** Zscaler reserves the right to monitor use of the Offerings and the right to suspend or terminate your access due to violation of this Policy.

## End-of-Life for Zscaler Authentication Bridge Hardware

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/end-life-zab-hardware
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > EOS & EOL Announcements > End-of-Life for Zscaler Authentication Bridge Hardware
- Last modified: 2024-01-24T02:43Z
- Summary: End-of-Life (EOL) notice for the Zscaler Authentication Bridge (ZAB) hardware.

Zscaler will no longer support the Zscaler Authentication Bridge (ZAB) hardware as of March 1, 2019.

Support for the ZAB hardware will be permanently terminated after March 31, 2019.

The ZAB functionality is now available via software. To continue using ZAB, migrate to the ZAB software before March 1, 2019.

If you need help with the migration or if you have additional questions or concerns, contact Zscaler Support via the Support link in the Admin Portal.

Announcement date: December 20, 2017

## End-of-Sale & End-of-Life Notice for Zscaler Cloud Identity Entitlement Management

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/end-sale-and-end-life-notice-zscaler-cloud-identity-entitlement-management
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > EOS & EOL Announcements > End-of-Sale & End-of-Life Notice for Zscaler Cloud Identity Entitlement Management
- Last modified: 2022-08-19T07:00Z
- Summary: End-of-Sale (EOS) and End-of-Life (EOL) notice for Zscaler Cloud Identity Entitlement Management (CIEM).

Zscaler is announcing the End-of-Sale (EOS) and End-of-Life (EOL) dates for Zscaler Cloud Identity Entitlement Management (CIEM).

| EOS Date | EOL Date |
| --- | --- |
| October 18, 2022 | October 18, 2023 |

As of October 18, 2022, licenses for new CIEM subscriptions will not be available for purchase. The CIEM service and all existing tenants will continue to be supported until the EOL date.

## Next Steps

If you are using CIEM, you should consider a migration plan to Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC)—the new generation platform, covering CIEM functionality and multiple additional modules and features. The ZPC service is now available for CIEM customers with no extra charge for the remainder of the subscription period.

Contact Zscaler Support to devise a migration plan.

## Additional Information

To learn more about Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC), see [https://www.zscaler.com/products/posture-control](https://www.zscaler.com/products/posture-control). If you have additional questions, contact [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/phone-support).

Announcement date: July 18, 2022

| EOS Date | EOL Date |
| --- | --- |
| March 15, 2025 | March 15, 2026 |

## Next Steps

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/product-usage-terms/end-support-3des-ipsec","lastmod":"2024-03-22T03:17Z","nid":"1269836"} -->
## End-of-Support for 3DES on IPSec

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/end-support-3des-ipsec
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > EOS & EOL Announcements > End-of-Support for 3DES on IPSec
- Last modified: 2024-03-22T03:17Z
- Summary: End-of-Support (EOS) notice for 3DES for IPSec.

Zscaler no longer supports 3DES for IPSec encryption (IKE Phase 2 only), as documented in the 5.4 Late-July Patch Release Notes.

Zscaler recommends that you use null encryption for your IPSec tunnels to the Zscaler service. Traffic sent to the internet does not require additional encryption. Sensitive content is currently encrypted using TLS between the client and the destination server.

If you must encrypt traffic using IPSec (for regulatory or compliance reasons), and you have the appropriate entitlement, use AES encryption.

If you need help changing your configuration or if you have additional questions or concerns, contact Zscaler Support via the Support link in the Admin Portal.

Announcement date: August 25, 2017
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/product-usage-terms/end-support-3des-ssl","lastmod":"2022-07-18T10:25Z","nid":"1270006"} -->
## End-of-Support for 3DES on SSL

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/end-support-3des-ssl
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > EOS & EOL Announcements > End-of-Support for 3DES on SSL
- Last modified: 2022-07-18T10:25Z
- Summary: End-of-Support (EOS) notice for 3DES for SSL.

Zscaler will end support of 3DES for SSL after the 5.6 release. If you have clients using 3DES for SSL, ensure that they change it to AES256-GCM-SHA384, AES128-GCM-SHA256, AES256-SHA, or AES128-SHA by October 31, 2018.

If you do not change it, clients using 3DES will be unable to connect to websites when 3DES support is ended.

If you need help changing your configuration or if you have additional questions or concerns, contact Zscaler Support via the Support link in the Admin Portal.

Announcement date: September 13, 2017
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/product-usage-terms/end-support-adobe-flash-cookies","lastmod":"2022-07-18T10:23Z","nid":"1269016"} -->
## End-of-Support for Adobe Flash Cookies

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/end-support-adobe-flash-cookies
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > EOS & EOL Announcements > End-of-Support for Adobe Flash Cookies
- Last modified: 2022-07-18T10:23Z
- Summary: End-of-Support (EOS) for Adobe Flash cookies.

In our continuing effort to provide the highest level of security to our users, Zscaler is discontinuing its use of Adobe Flash cookies on its authentication pages and pre-provisioned cookies as an authentication mechanism. This is due to security concerns around the vulnerabilities of Adobe Flash cookies.

## Determine If You Are Using Adobe Flash Cookies

You are using Adobe Flash cookies if you downloaded cookies from https://admin.<Zscaler Cloud Name>/download/cookies and distributed them to your users’ devices. To find your Zscaler cloud name, see [What is my cloud name for ZIA?](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/what-my-cloud-name-zia)

## What to Do

If you are using Adobe Flash cookies for authentication, ensure that another authentication mechanism is configured on the Authentication Settings page of the ZIA Admin Portal. Zscaler recommends deploying Identity Federation using SAML for provisioning and authentication. To learn more, see [Choosing Provisioning and Authentication Methods](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/choosing-provisioning-and-authentication-methods).

You can also deploy the Zscaler Client Connector to your users with no additional charge. The Zscaler Client Connector provides all of the benefits of the Zscaler Cloud Security Platform for internet traffic, and requires users to log in just once. To learn more, see [What is the Zscaler Client Connector?](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/what-zscaler-app)

If you do not configure an authentication mechanism before Zscaler ends its support for Adobe Flash cookies, the Zscaler service will use the authentication mechanism that is already configured on the ZIA Admin Portal to authenticate users.

Additionally, Zscaler strongly recommends that you inform your users about the new authentication process, because the Adobe Flash cookies allowed them to skip the authentication step. With the new authentication mechanism, users will need to authenticate themselves to the Zscaler service at least once.

## Change Timing

Zscaler discontinued its support for Adobe Flash cookies in the 5.5 release.

## Additional Information

If you need help changing your configuration or if you have additional questions or concerns, contact Zscaler Support via the Support link in the ZIA Admin Portal.

Announcement date: August 14, 2017
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## End-of-Support for CentOS 7.x, RHEL 7.x, and Oracle Linux 7.x

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/end-support-centos-7.x-rhel-7.x-and-oracle-linux-7.x
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > EOS & EOL Announcements > End-of-Support for CentOS 7.x, RHEL 7.x, and Oracle Linux 7.x
- Last modified: 2026-06-17T15:48Z
- Summary: End-of-Support for CentOS 7.x, RHEL 7.x, and Oracle Linux 7.x

Zscaler will no longer support App Connectors and Private Service Edges running on CentOS 7.x, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.x (RHEL 7.x), and Oracle Linux 7.x after March 31, 2025. Customers currently using CentOS 7.x, RHEL 7.x, Oracle Linux 7.x, and the EL7 ZPA repository will need to migrate to Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 or later and the EL9 ZPA repository after this date.

To learn more, see [Zscaler Selects Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 (RHEL 9) as Next-Gen Private Access Operating System](https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/product-insights/zscaler-selects-red-hat-enterprise-linux-9-rhel-9-next-gen-private-access).

If you need help migrating to Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 or later, or if you have additional questions or concerns, contact Zscaler Support.

Announcement date: February 9, 2024

Revised date: December 9, 2024
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/product-usage-terms/end-support-certificate-downloads","lastmod":"2023-08-12T07:06Z","nid":"1457531"} -->
## End-of-Support for Certificate Downloads

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/end-support-certificate-downloads
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > EOS & EOL Announcements > End-of-Support for Certificate Downloads
- Last modified: 2023-08-12T07:06Z
- Summary: End-of-Support (EOS) notice for Zscaler Client Connector Certificate Downloads.

Versions of Zscaler Client Connector 2.1 and earlier downloaded the configured SSL inspection certificate from a cloud-based content delivery network (CDN). While version 2.1 is no longer supported, this notice is to inform you that as of September 1, 2023, the certificate download function will be removed.

Devices still running version 2.1 or earlier will continue to function, however if the SSL certificate is not trusted by the device, it will not be downloaded.

Ensure you're running the latest supported versions of Zscaler Client Connector. To learn more, see [Supported Versions](https://help.zscaler.com/eos-eol/supported-versions).

Announcement date: July 11, 2023
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/product-usage-terms/end-support-client-certificate-posture-check-and-device-admin-samsung-android-devices","lastmod":"2026-06-11T14:09Z","nid":"1462086"} -->
## End-of-Support for the Client Certificate Posture Check and Device Admin for Samsung Android Devices

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/end-support-client-certificate-posture-check-and-device-admin-samsung-android-devices
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > EOS & EOL Announcements > End-of-Support for the Client Certificate Posture Check and Device Admin for Samsung Android Devices
- Last modified: 2026-06-11T14:09Z
- Summary: End-of-Support (EOS) notice for Zscaler Client Connector Client Certificate Posture check and Device Admin for for Samsung Android Devices

An update has been made to this announcement. To learn more, see [End-of-Support for the Client Certificate Posture Type for All Android Devices.](https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/end-support-client-certificate-posture-type-all-android-devices)

With the release of Zscaler Client Connector version 1.13 for Android, Device Admin support will be removed for new installations. Upgrades of previous releases will include Device Admin until the release of Zscaler Client Connector version 1.14 for Android, which will no longer support Device Admin for new installs and upgrades. The installation parameter enableKnox will also be removed with the release of Zscaler Client Connector version 1.14 for Android.

Zscaler recommends you remove the Client Certificate posture check for Android in the Zscaler Client Connector Portal. You can continue to use Device Admin and the Client Certificate posture check until you log out of Zscaler Client Connector after upgrading to Zscaler Client Connector version 1.13 for Android.

### Next Steps

If you are currently using the Client Certificate posture check for your Samsung Android devices, adjust your Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) access policy to remove these checks, so that new installs of Zscaler Client Connector version 1.13 and later for Android and upgrades to Zscaler Client Connector version 1.14 for Android don't break ZPA policy access on Android.

Announcement date: August 9, 2023
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

## End-of-Support for the Client Certificate Posture Type for All Android Devices

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/end-support-client-certificate-posture-type-all-android-devices
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > EOS & EOL Announcements > End-of-Support for the Client Certificate Posture Type for All Android Devices

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/product-usage-terms/end-support-sms-otp-authentication-zidentity","lastmod":"2026-07-09T07:06Z","nid":"1539653"} -->
## End-of-Support for SMS OTP Authentication in Authentication Service

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/end-support-sms-otp-authentication-zidentity
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > EOS & EOL Announcements > End-of-Support for SMS OTP Authentication in Authentication Service
- Last modified: 2026-07-09T07:06Z
- Summary: Information on end-of-support for SMS-based authentication in Authentication Service

As of August 07, 2026, Authentication Service will no longer support SMS-based one-time passcodes (OTP) for multi-factor authentication (MFA) for hosted users and hosted admins. This change strengthens Authentication Service's MFA posture as per the NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-63B guidance, which classifies SMS or voice delivered over the public switched telephone network (PSTN) as a RESTRICTED method for out-of-band authentication.

To learn more, see [NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.3.3 - Authentication using the Public Switched Telephone Network](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html#:~:text=5.1.3.3%20Authentication%20using%20the%20Public%20Switched%20Telephone%20Network) and [NIST SP 800-63B §5.2.10 - Restricted Authenticators](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html#:~:text=5.2.10%20Restricted%20Authenticators).

## Key Dates

| Date | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| May 22, 2026 | SMS MFA enrollment will no longer be available for new tenants created post the announcement date. Existing admins and users already using SMS MFA are not impacted at this stage. These admins and users will be prompted to choose another available MFA method. |
| August 07, 2026 | SMS MFA will be disabled for sign-in. Admins and users attempting to use SMS will be guided to set up another available MFA method during sign-in. |

## Action

Make sure that all the impacted admins and users in your organization have transitioned to another available MFA method before August 07, 2026, to avoid any disruption during sign-in.

If you have additional questions, [contact Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support).

Announcement date: May 20, 2026
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/product-usage-terms/eos-and-eol-policy","lastmod":"2025-02-03T07:01Z","nid":"1269766"} -->
## EOS and EOL Policy

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/eos-and-eol-policy
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > Software Policy & Support > EOS and EOL Policy
- Last modified: 2025-02-03T07:01Z
- Summary: Description of the Zscaler End-of-Sale (EOS) and End-of-Life (EOL) policies.

This policy is effective as of August 1st, 2017.

Zscaler services and products (collectively the “Products”) are continuously improved and earlier versions of the Products may reach their End-of-Life (EOL) as new versions of the Products supersede them. This policy is a guide for customers and partners regarding the milestones and timeframes for when a Product reaches EOL. This policy is provided to assist customers and partners in planning and successfully transitioning to current versions of the Products or new Products, and covers the following three areas:

1. Zscaler SaaS Products
2. Zscaler Software Products
3. Zscaler Hardware

## Zscaler SaaS Products

Zscaler SaaS Products are upgraded regularly with the current version replacing the previous version in the Zscaler cloud. Zscaler upgrades all customers together in its cloud, so all customers maintain the most current supported version. However, a specific SaaS Product might transition through milestones to its EOL.

| SaaS Products Milestones | Timeframe | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| End-of-Sale (EOS) | Zscaler notification at least 90 days before EOS | SaaS Product is no longer available for new orders. However, the SaaS Product may be renewed to extend an existing contract or to add more users through its EOL date. Zscaler will continue to provide support for the Product until the EOL for the Product. |
| End-of-Life (EOL) | EOL at least 1 year after the EOS date | After EOL, the SaaS Product will no longer be available and customers with existing contracts that extend beyond the EOL date will be offered either an upgrade path or replacement or Zscaler will support the current Product until the end of the then-current contract term without renewal. |

## Zscaler Software Products

Over time, Zscaler Software Products that are installed on user devices may be superseded by newer versions or Products, and the latest supported versions are published for customers and partners at [Supported Versions](https://help.zscaler.com/eos-eol/announcements/supported-versions). Customers and partners are encouraged to use the latest supported versions.

### Zscaler Software Support Policy

In general, Zscaler supports the latest Software version and the two previous versions for each Software Product. In some cases, Zscaler may designate another version as a supported version and will note this at [Supported Versions](https://help.zscaler.com/eos-eol/announcements/supported-versions). Software Product [Supported Versions](https://help.zscaler.com/eos-eol/announcements/supported-versions) are eligible for patch and maintenance upgrades until the EOL of the Product.

Zscaler Support will request that customers and partners upgrade to a [Supported Version](https://help.zscaler.com/eos-eol/announcements/supported-versions) before beginning troubleshooting. Support services transfer to the supported versions of the Software.

In some cases, an organization may elect to use a Software Product version that is no longer recommended or supported by Zscaler. Zscaler will provide information regarding the status of Software versions at [Supported Versions](https://help.zscaler.com/eos-eol/announcements/supported-versions) so that customers and partners can make informed choices about which version to use in their organization.

| Software Products Milestones | Timeframe | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| End-of-Sale (EOS) | Zscaler notification at least 60 days before EOS | EOS Software Products are no longer available for purchase or download by customers or partners. Supported Versions of EOS Software Products are eligible for patch and maintenance upgrades until the EOL of the Product. |
| End-of-Life (EOL) | EOL at least 6 months after the EOS date | After EOL, the Software Product is no longer eligible for patch or maintenance upgrades or support, and no longer has any supported versions. Existing contracts for Software Products that extend beyond the EOL date will be offered either an upgrade path to a replacement Software Product or Zscaler will support the EOL Software Product through the end of the then-current contract term without renewal. |

## Zscaler Hardware

To maintain cloud standards and support new technologies for customers and partners that lease hardware as part of the Zscaler solution, Zscaler initiates the replacement of Zscaler-owned hardware, whether it is in a third party datacenter or on-premises at a customer or partner site. This is called Hardware Refresh. Hardware Refresh is a necessary component of maintaining the operation of Zscaler Products and is done in coordination with customers and partners as part of the Zscaler Hardware Refresh Lifecycle described below. Customers and partners are notified of hardware refresh dates according the following table.

| Hardware Refresh Cycle | Timeframe | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Refresh Date | In most cases, about 5 years from the subscription start date for the Zscaler-owned hardware | The Refresh Date is the date by which Zscaler-owned hardware is to be replaced. Usually this is about 5 years from the subscription start date; however, Zscaler may refresh hardware at any time to support new innovations. |
| Refresh Notification | Zscaler notification at least 90 days before Refresh Date | Refresh Notification is a communication from Zscaler to customers and partners with the recommended Zscaler-owned new hardware shipment date and prior hardware return date. The specific shipment and return dates are then determined in consultation with the customer or partners. In some cases, upgrades may be expedited in order to support new functionality. |
| Refresh Shipment Date | Date new Zscaler-owned hardware is shipped | Date new Zscaler-owned equipment is shipped. It is recommended that the Refresh Shipment Date be prior to the Refresh Date of the hardware to be replaced. |
| Hardware Return Date | Unless otherwise agreed to by Zscaler, a maximum of 90 days after the Refresh Shipment Date | The Hardware Return Date is the date by which the replaced hardware is due to be received by Zscaler. Zscaler Service Level Agreements (SLAs) will not be available to Products running on hardware being used after its Hardware Return Date. At Zscaler’s option, hardware not returned to Zscaler within 90 days from the Hardware Return Date may be subject to additional asset recovery mitigation. |
| End-of-Life (EOL) | EOL 1 year after Refresh Date | Specific hardware may have an EOL date, which is the latest date the hardware can be used in production. SLAs are not available to Products running on hardware being used after its EOL date. Unless there is an urgent reason to refresh sooner, the EOL date will be 1 year after the Refresh Date. |

## General Disclaimer for All Products

SUBJECT TO THE ABOVE DETAILS WHERE USE OF THE PRODUCTS IS PERMITTED AFTER AN EOL DATE, ZSCALER SHALL NOT BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIMS OR DAMAGES IF CUSTOMER USES THE PRODUCTS PAST THE EOL DATE, OR THE HARDWARE RETURN DATE FOR HARDWARE, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO DEGRADATION OR INTERRUPTION OF THE PRODUCTS, AND SUCH USE PAST THE EOL DATE OR HARDWARE RETURN DATE SHALL RESULT IN THE INVALIDATION OF ANY AND ALL SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENTS AND SERVICE CREDITS FOR THE PRODUCTS.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## End-of-Sale & End-of-Life Notice for Zscaler SecureAgent on iOS

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/eos-eol-notice-zscaler-secureagent-ios
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > EOS & EOL Announcements > End-of-Sale & End-of-Life Notice for Zscaler SecureAgent on iOS
- Last modified: 2022-07-18T10:02Z
- Summary: End-of-Sale (EOS) and End-of-Life (EOL) notice for Zscaler SecureAgent on iOS.

Zscaler is announcing the End-of-Sale (EOS) and End-of-Life (EOL) dates for Zscaler SecureAgent for iOS. SecureAgent on iOS uses an on-demand IPSec VPN tunnel as its primary method to forward traffic to the Zscaler cloud from an Apple iOS device. This also includes agent-less IPSec-based deployment using advanced API-based integration with MDM partners, such as MobileIron and AirWatch.

| EOS Date | EOL Date |
| --- | --- |
| March 1, 2017 | November 30, 2017 |

As of March 1, 2017, user licenses for new deployments of iOS devices with Zscaler SecureAgent for iOS are not available for purchase.

Existing deployments of iOS with Global HTTP Proxy without using IPSec tunnels will be supported until EOL of Zscaler SecureAgent for iOS on November 30, 2017.

## Next Steps

If you are using SecureAgent on iOS devices with IPSec tunnels, you must plan a migration to Zscaler Client Connector for iOS. You must migrate to Zscaler Client Connector on iOS by November 30, 2017, as Zscaler SecureAgent for iOS will be EOL and no longer supported.

## Additional Information

If you have additional questions, contact Zscaler Support via the Support link in the Admin Portal.

Announcement date: July 20, 2017
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/product-usage-terms/hardware-rma","lastmod":"2026-05-14T15:30Z","nid":"1539912"} -->
## Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) Process and Policy

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/hardware-rma
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > Hardware Usage Terms > Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) Process and Policy
- Last modified: 2026-05-14T15:30Z
- Summary: Information about Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) Process and Policy.

This RMA Process and Policy applies to all Zscaler Hardware.

To initiate the Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) process, submit a support ticket via the [Zscaler Support Portal](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support). Zscaler Support works with you to troubleshoot and diagnose issues remotely. If the issue cannot be resolved remotely or is determined to be a Hardware fault, Zscaler might decide to replace the Hardware.

Zscaler Support does the following to continue the RMA process:

1. Requests the following information:
  1. Company Name
  2. Organization ID (Org ID)
  3. Shipping Address
  4. Contact name, phone number, and email address
  5. Product model, serial, and asset tag numbers
2. Creates an RMA number for tracking purposes.
3. Ships a replacement device to you.

A return shipping label is included with the replacement device in most cases. You must package the defective device and ship it to Zscaler within 30 calendar days of receiving the replacement device. All returned items must have a valid Zscaler RMA number. This number is crucial to ensure the accurate tracking and handling of returned items. For any questions related to RMA or shipping, contact your Zscaler support representative.

Do not return any Hardware until an RMA is issued.

The RMA process is complete after the replacement device is successfully installed and operational and Zscaler receives the defective device.

###### Data Removal Obligations

You acknowledge and agree that it is your responsibility to remove any and all data before shipping or disposing of your devices. Zscaler is not responsible for the security, safeguarding, or return of any data left on devices that have been shipped to or disposed of by Zscaler.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/product-usage-terms/hardware-usage-terms-policy","lastmod":"2026-08-12T17:15Z","nid":"1539906"} -->
## Hardware Usage Terms

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/hardware-usage-terms-policy
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > Hardware Usage Terms > Hardware Usage Terms
- Last modified: 2026-08-12T17:15Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Hardware Usage Terms.

If your Order includes Hardware, the following terms apply. For product-specific requirements, refer to the applicable Product-Specific Hardware Terms below.

###### 1. Ownership and Use Rights

**1.1.** All Hardware is and shall remain the property of Zscaler during and after the Subscription Term. You acquire no ownership interest in the Hardware.

**1.2.** You shall not sell, lease, transfer, or repurpose the Hardware, or permit any third party to use the Hardware for any purpose.

**1.3.** You may install and use the Hardware solely at your premises, data center(s), or authorized partner locations for the purpose of enabling your authorized use of the applicable Zscaler service in accordance with the Documentation.

###### 2. Use Restrictions

**2.1.** You shall not, and shall not permit any third party to:

a. Load, install, or run any software on the Hardware other than software provided or authorized by Zscaler;

b. Make any physical alterations or additions to the Hardware;

c. Attempt to repair, service, or maintain the Hardware except as expressly instructed by Zscaler;

d. Reverse engineer, disassemble, or decompile the Hardware or any software therein;

e. Without Zscaler's prior written consent, permit any person other than Zscaler or Zscaler-authorized agents to access, open, or service the Hardware; or

f. Relocate the Hardware from one physical location to another without prior written approval from Zscaler.

**2.2.** You shall handle all Hardware with reasonable care and shall not subject the Hardware to misuse, abuse, neglect, or mishandling.

###### 3. Delivery and Installation

**3.1.** Zscaler shall suitably pack and ship Hardware to the address specified by you in the applicable Order.

**3.2.** You shall provide a local point of contact for delivery, accurate shipping information, and any assistance or cooperation required for customs clearance.

**3.3.** Zscaler shall not be liable for shipping delays caused by customs processing, regulatory compliance, carrier delays, or other factors beyond Zscaler's reasonable control.

**3.4.** If delivery fails due to incorrect shipping information provided by you, your refusal of delivery, or your failure to provide a local contact, all costs incurred by Zscaler (including storage, return shipment, and re-delivery) shall be reimbursed by you.

**3.5.** You shall perform physical installation of Hardware in accordance with Zscaler's specifications and Documentation, unless otherwise specified in the applicable Product-Specific Hardware Terms.

###### 4. Customer Obligations

**4.1. Technical Representative.** You shall appoint at least one technical representative with physical access to the Hardware and authority to grant Zscaler or its authorized agents physical access to the Hardware location. Your technical representative shall respond to Zscaler requests within a commercially reasonable timeframe.

**4.2. Environment.** You shall, at your expense:

a. Maintain the Hardware in an environment that meets Zscaler's operating conditions for the applicable Hardware, including temperature, humidity, and other environmental conditions as specified in the Documentation; and

b. Provide continuous, uninterrupted power supply to the Hardware with suitable surge protection.

**4.3. Device Count and Capacity.** You shall maintain a sufficient number of Hardware units as recommended by Zscaler. If Zscaler determines that your traffic or usage exceeds Hardware capacity, you shall, within thirty (30) days of notification, accommodate additional or upgraded Hardware or take action to reduce utilization in accordance with Zscaler's guidance.

**4.4.** If you relocate Hardware with Zscaler's prior written authorization, you shall be responsible for all associated costs, including licenses, permits, shipping, VAT, taxes, and applicable duties.

###### 5. Maintenance and Updates

**5.1.** During the Subscription Term, Zscaler shall provide remote management, monitoring, and maintenance for all Hardware. Zscaler may update, upgrade, or replace Hardware at its sole discretion.

###### 6. Repair and Replacement

**6.1.** If Hardware fails or becomes defective during the Subscription Term, Zscaler shall provide advance replacement Hardware, subject to availability.

**6.2.** Zscaler will ship replacement Hardware within one (1) to three (3) business days of confirming the failure.

**6.3.** All Hardware repairs and replacements are subject to Zscaler's [Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA)](https://help.zscaler.com/eos-eol/return-merchandise-authorization-rma-process-and-policy) process. You shall not return Hardware without first obtaining an RMA number from Zscaler.

**6.4.** Upon receipt of replacement Hardware, you shall return defective Hardware to Zscaler within thirty (30) calendar days using the return instructions provided by Zscaler.

**6.5.** You shall perform physical setup of replacement Hardware in accordance with Zscaler's instructions, unless otherwise specified in the applicable Product-Specific Hardware Terms.

**6.6.** You are responsible for removing all data from Hardware prior to returning or disposing of the Hardware. Zscaler is not responsible for the security or return of any data remaining on Hardware returned to or disposed of by you.

###### 7. Return Upon Termination or Expiration of Subscription Term

**7.1.** Upon termination or expiration of the Subscription Term, you shall return all Hardware to Zscaler within twenty-one (21) calendar days.

**7.2.** Zscaler shall provide an RMA number, return packaging and shipping instructions. Zscaler shall bear the cost of return shipping. In cases where return is not cost-effective due to the age of the Hardware or shipping costs, Zscaler may instruct you to dispose of the Hardware in accordance with your internal disposal policies. You shall provide Zscaler with a Certificate of Destruction and shall bear any costs associated with such disposal.

**7.3.** If you fail to return Hardware within twenty-one (21) calendar days of termination or expiration, Zscaler may invoice you for the replacement value of such Hardware and may engage authorized contractors to retrieve the Hardware at your expense.

**7.4. Evaluation Hardware.** If Hardware was provided for evaluation, proof of concept, or trial purposes, you shall either (a) return the Hardware to Zscaler within twenty-one (21) calendar days following the end of the evaluation period, or (b) convert to a paid production subscription for the applicable Zscaler service before the end of the evaluation period. If you do not return the Hardware or convert to a paid subscription, Sections 7.3 and 9.1 apply.

###### 8. Exclusions

**8.1.** Zscaler's obligations under these Hardware Usage Terms do not apply to:

**a.** Hardware, software, or components not provided by Zscaler;

**b.** Hardware that has been modified, altered, or serviced by anyone other than Zscaler or Zscaler-authorized agents;

**c.** Hardware used beyond the useful life advised by Zscaler;

**d.** Damage caused by events or conditions beyond Zscaler's reasonable control, including fire, flood, earthquake, power surge, or other force majeure events;

**e.** Hardware used or stored in an environment that does not meet Zscaler's published specifications;

**f.** Hardware obtained from any source other than directly from Zscaler or an authorized Zscaler Partner; or

**g.** Situations in which you are unresponsive or unwilling to cooperate with Zscaler's reasonable requests for access, information, or assistance.

###### 9. Remedies and Enforcement

**9.1. Contractor Engagement.** If you are unresponsive or unwilling to assist with installation, troubleshooting, maintenance, or return of Hardware, Zscaler may engage authorized contractors to perform such tasks. You shall reimburse Zscaler for all reasonable costs incurred.

**9.2. Service Level Agreements.** Your failure to comply with any obligation under these Hardware Usage Terms, including the applicable Product-Specific Hardware Terms, shall result in the invalidation of any and all related Service Level Agreements for the affected Zscaler service.

## Product-Specific Hardware Terms

The following Product-Specific Hardware Terms supplement the Hardware Usage Terms and apply to the specific Hardware identified in your Order. In the event of a conflict, the Product-Specific Hardware Terms control for the applicable Hardware.

###### A. Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) Appliances

For the purpose of Section A, the term "Hardware" should mean the hardware provided by Zscaler to you as Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) appliances. The following additional terms apply if your Order includes Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) appliances:

**A.1. Minimum Device Count.** You shall maintain no fewer than two (2) Hardware units per installation location.

**A.2. Internet Redundancy.** You shall provide internet connectivity through no fewer than two (2) discrete internet service providers with redundant capabilities at each installation location.

**A.3. 24/7 Technical Staff.** You shall ensure that personnel capable of responding to Zscaler requests and providing physical access to the Hardware are available 24 hours per day, 7 days per week.

**A.4. Installation and Setup.** You are responsible for the physical installation of Hardware in accordance with Zscaler's published instructions. Zscaler Cloud Operations will manage the configuration and ongoing operation of the Hardware.

**A.5. Maintenance Windows.** You shall notify Zscaler of any scheduled maintenance windows that may affect the operation or connectivity of the Hardware.

**A.6. Connectivity and Network Configuration.** You shall: (a) Provide and maintain dedicated internet connectivity sufficient for the Hardware to communicate with the Zscaler cloud; (b) Configure firewall and network settings in compliance with Zscaler's published requirements; and (c) Provide and maintain all required IP addresses, DNS settings, and network resources as specified by Zscaler.

**A.7. Repair and Replacement.** The repair and replacement process for the Hardware is managed by Zscaler Cloud Operations. Zscaler will coordinate replacement directly with you in accordance with the procedures described in the applicable support documentation.

###### B. Zero Trust Branch Appliances

For the purpose of Section B, the term "Hardware" should mean the hardware provided by Zscaler to you as Zero Trust Branch appliances. The following additional terms apply if your Order includes Zero Trust Branch appliances:

**B.1. 24/7 Availability.** You shall ensure personnel with physical access to the Hardware are available to respond to Zscaler requests 24 hours per day, 7 days per week.

**B.2. Technical Representative Training.** Your technical representative shall be fully trained, at your expense, on the Hardware's basic specifications and operational requirements through Zscaler-provided or Zscaler-approved documentation.

**B.3. Remote Connectivity.** You shall provide Zscaler with remote connectivity access to the Hardware for management and troubleshooting purposes.

**B.4. Customer Setup.** You are responsible for the physical setup and rack-mounting (if applicable) of the Hardware in accordance with Zscaler's published instructions.

**B.5. Connectivity and Network Configuration.** You shall: (a) Provide and maintain dedicated internet connectivity sufficient for the Hardware to communicate with the Zscaler cloud; (b) Configure firewall and network settings in compliance with Zscaler's published requirements; and (c) Provide and maintain all required IP addresses, DNS settings, and network resources as specified by Zscaler.

###### C. Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Appliances

For the purpose of Section C, the term "Hardware" should mean the hardware provided by Zscaler to you as Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) appliances. The following additional terms apply if your Order includes Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) appliances:

**C.1. 24/7 Availability.** You shall ensure personnel with physical access to the Hardware are available to respond to Zscaler requests 24 hours per day, 7 days per week.

**C.2. Technical Representative Training.** Your technical representative shall be fully trained, at your expense, on the Hardware's basic specifications and operational requirements through Zscaler-provided or Zscaler-approved documentation.

**C.3. Remote Connectivity.** You shall provide Zscaler with remote connectivity access to the Hardware for management and troubleshooting purposes.

**C.4. Customer Setup.** You are responsible for the physical setup and rack-mounting (if applicable) of the Hardware in accordance with Zscaler's published instructions.

## Zscaler Client Connector Supported Versions

Zscaler supports the latest software version and the two previous versions for each software product. For Zscaler Client Connector, Zscaler also supports the current Long-Term Support (LTS) version. In some cases, Zscaler might designate another version as a supported version. To learn more about LTS, see [Zscaler Client Connector Long-Term Support](https://help.zscaler.com/eos-eol/zscaler-client-connector-long-term-support).

The following endpoint application versions are currently supported based on the OS:

- Windows
- macOS
- Linux
- iOS
- Android
- Android on ChromeOS

Zscaler limits the enrollment of devices or the transmission to the Zscaler cloud from unsupported releases. To learn more, see the Deprecation of Enrollment for Outdated Zscaler Client Connector Releases [trust post](https://trust.zscaler.com/zscaler.net/posts/25466).

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/product-usage-terms/zscaler-client-connector-long-term-support","lastmod":"2025-12-10T15:52Z","nid":"1528461"} -->
## Zscaler Client Connector Long-Term Support

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/zscaler-client-connector-long-term-support
- Product: Product Usage Terms & Policies
- Path: Product Usage Terms & Policies > Software Policy & Support > Zscaler Client Connector Long-Term Support
- Last modified: 2025-12-10T15:52Z
- Summary: Long-Term Support for Zscaler Client Connector

This policy is effective as of January 31, 2025.

## What is Long-Term Support?

In addition to supporting the current and previous two versions of Zscaler Client Connector for each of the desktop OS platforms, Zscaler identifies one of those [specific versions](https://help.zscaler.com/eos-eol/supported-versions) per desktop OS platform as the Long-Term Support (LTS) version. LTS means that the selected version of Zscaler Client Connector is supported for up to 12 months from the date of the LTS announcement, regardless of how the set of supported versions continues to change.

The LTS version is not updated with new features and functionality during those 12 months. However, there could be new releases based on that LTS version which are made available to customers to fix bugs and security issues.

Each LTS version is chosen based on widespread customer adoption.

## Which platforms does LTS apply to?

Currently, LTS only applies to Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms. As Zscaler Client Connector for iOS and Zscaler Client Connector for Android on ChromeOS are typically deployed from their respective app stores, it is not possible to maintain multiple versions.

## Why is the LTS version needed?

As Zscaler Client Connector is a widely adopted security solution, it is critical that newer versions are adopted. Zscaler recognizes that the frequency of updates might not apply to all deployments. Such environments face the challenge of complying with these change controls while running software versions that are supported by their vendors. Zscaler provides customers with the choice of deploying LTS versions that continue to be updated with security and bug fixes, but not with new functionality so that their environments can remain protected with minimal software churn.

## Is this the recommended version?

In general, no. LTS is intended to give Zscaler customers a stable version to run for an extended period of time. The recommended version is typically the latest version that has reached General Availability (GA). If your environment has a requirement for longer change cycles that prevent more frequent updates to GA versions, then Zscaler recommends the LTS version for you.

## How will changes to future LTS versions happen?

Two months prior to the next LTS version, the projected next version is announced, giving time for customers to migrate to the latest LTS version.

As LTS is chosen from existing versions, the next LTS is a version already available for tenants.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/troubleshooting-runbooks/access-denied-due-bad-server-certificate","lastmod":"2026-07-29T15:28Z","nid":"1538845"} -->
## Access Denied Due to Bad Server Certificate

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/access-denied-due-bad-server-certificate
- Product: Zscaler Support Troubleshooting Runbooks
- Path: Zscaler Support Troubleshooting Runbooks > Internet & SaaS Access Control Policies Troubleshooting Runbook > SSL Inspection Issues > Access Denied Due to Bad Server Certificate
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T15:28Z
- Summary: This article describes how to check why Internet & SaaS access policies deny a URL due to a bad server certificate.

This issue implies the following scenarios for the website's server certificate:

- The server does not present the complete certificate chain during the SSL handshake.
- The certificate shows as revoked in the OCSP revocation check.
- The certificate is expired.
- The certificate is self-signed.

The website has to provide all the intermediate certificates in the chain, because Zscaler does not manually add intermediate certifications to its trust store. Only trust anchors (i.e., root CA certificates are stored in the trust stores of our nodes). The following is generally how the chain validation happens for a simple scenario with only three certificates in a chain:

1. The **Common Name (CN)**, or one of the **Subject Alternative Names (SAN)** in the website's certificate, must match the domain part of the URL.
2. The issuer's value in the website's certificate must match the CN in the intermediate issuer's certificate.
3. Then, the issuer value in the intermediate issuer's certificate must match the CN in the root certificate.

The following is an example where the chain validation fails because the chain is complete, but the names don't match as mentioned above:

1. 1st cert CN: ipma-wa.com, issuer: Network Solutions RSA DV SSL CA 3
2. 2nd cert CN: Network Solutions DV Server CA 2, Issuer: USERTrust RSA Certification Authority
3. 3rd cert CN: USERTrust RSA Certification Authority, issuer: USERTrust RSA Certification Authority

The chain is broken because the server certification is issued by Network Solutions RSA DV SSL CA 3, but the chain includes the intermediate cert of Network Solutions DV Server CA 2.

Zscaler uses OCSP stapling to obtain the revocation status of a certificate. When enabled in the SSL Inspection policy, the Internet & SaaS Service Edge checks the revocation status of the certificate regardless of other certificate attributes. If the issuing CA revokes the certificate, the Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS treats the certificate as untrusted. The action for such transactions is determined by the Untrusted Server Certificates configuration.

## Troubleshooting

The following are troubleshooting steps:

1. Try to access the website without Zscaler in the path and observe the SSL handshake.
2. Use an external tool to validate the server's SSL configuration.
3. When the Zscaler Service Edge either cannot complete the handshake with a web server or detects the certificate as untrusted or bad, it's best to cross-validate certain attributes of the public website's SSL configuration. To learn more, see [How to Validate the SSL Configuration of a Web Server](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/how-validate-ssl-configuration-web-server).
4. Look at the Web log values for the following columns:
  - **Certificate Chain Validity**: If the value is **Fail**, then it's very likely that this web server is not serving the complete chain during the SSL handshake. Typically, these issues can be fixed at the source if the web server's configuration can be rectified to send the complete chain from all the applicable servers. If you see that some transactions for the same domain show **Pass**or **Fail**in this column when passing through the same DC, it could be due to one of the following reasons :
    - When the full chain is not presented by the server, if you have the intermediate certificate present in our intermediate CA cert cache, you verify the chain and allow the connection.
    - Sometimes the web service is served by multiple physical servers hidden behind a single VIP. If some of those physical servers are configured to serve the complete chain while some are not, you might also see this behavior.
    - How do I validate the server certificate configured in one specific physical server? You can specify the server IP using a syntax similar to this: `https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/analyze.html?d=xyz.com&s=11.11.11.11&latest.`In this case, the tool validates the certificates configured in the server at 11.11.11.11 for the website xyz.com.
    - Some websites are configured to provide more than one trust chains. One of these chains may have a configuration problem.
    - These issues are sometimes not seen without Zscaler because some web browsers are configured to perform [AIA fetching](https://www.thesslstore.com/blog/aia-fetching) to fix the incomplete certificate chain, which hides the certificate chain issues from the end user.
  - **Server Certificate Self Signed**: This field's value must not be **Yes**. The SME verifies the server certificate against a preinstalled list of certificate authorities. Self-signed certificates are considered untrusted.
  - **Certificate Expiry**: If the value is **Yes**, then that's the reason the certificate was marked bad. Verify that the current date lies between the **Issued on** and **Expires on** dates mentioned in the certificate.
  - **Server Connection OCSP Result**: If the value shows **Revoked**, that's why the certificate was considered bad.

## Solution

The following steps provide solution options:

- Zscaler recommends adding an SSL policy with a **Pass Through** action for untrusted certificates or configure allow policy for a given URL only if it's trusted by your business. In this case, any warnings related to the certificate is passed through to the end user.
- If the error is shown because the OCSP check fails for the certificate, the customer can choose to disable OCSP check in the SSL policy rule for a specific domain (but Zscaler does not recommend this action).
- If none of the above helps understand the problem, submit a case to [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support) with the following information:
  - If [**Remote Assistance** is enabled](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/enabling-remote-assistance), the URL and the timestamp when a user tried accessing the web application via Zscaler. Otherwise, the Web Insights logs showing all the columns for the relevant transactions.
  - A screenshot of the error seen in the browser or the application.
  - Any detailed error messages or application logs, if available.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/troubleshooting-runbooks/access-denied-due-domain-fronting","lastmod":"2026-07-29T15:27Z","nid":"1538961"} -->
## Access Denied Due to Domain Fronting

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/access-denied-due-domain-fronting
- Product: Zscaler Support Troubleshooting Runbooks
- Path: Zscaler Support Troubleshooting Runbooks > Internet & SaaS Access Control Policies Troubleshooting Runbook > Web Access Issues > Access Denied Due to Domain Fronting
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T15:27Z
- Summary: In a domain fronting attack, the domain used in the Server Name Indication (SNI) extension or in the Connect request is different from the one supplied later in the Host header. In other words, an attacker hides an HTTP request for a bad website inside a TLS connection to a good website.

In a domain fronting attack, the domain used in Server Name Indication (SNI) extension or in the Connect request is different from the one supplied later in the Host header. In other words, an attacker hides an HTTP request to a bad website inside a TLS connection to a good website.

Whenever a URL is accessed by a browser or an application, that browser or application must initiate a TLS negotiation, known as a handshake, with the FQDN extracted from the URL. For example, if you enter `https://www.google.com/search?q=test` in a browser, the browser initiates a TLS handshake with the FQDN www.google.com.

After the TLS handshake is successful, the browser then specifies the actual HTTP server using the Host header in the HTTP request. Ideally, this Host value and the SNI FQDN are on the same parent domain, if not an exact match. In some cases, the FQDN specified in the Connect request might also be different from the Host header in the HTTP request.

## Troubleshooting

To troubleshoot the issue:

1. Validate that the **Block Domain Fronting** option under **Administration**> **Advanced Settings** is enabled and review the exemptions in that section. To learn more, see [Configuring Advanced Settings](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-advanced-settings#domain-fronting).
2. Review the values in the following Web Insights logs columns: **URL**, **Domain Fronted Host Header**, and **Domain Fronted SNI**.
3. If the URL value is different from either the **Domain Fronted SNI** or the **Domain Fronted Host Header** values, then the access is getting denied as configured. See image.
4. To cross-validate, take the following steps:
  1. If the **Domain Fronted SNI** shows an **FQDN**, take a packet capture using [Zscaler Client Connector](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/enabling-packet-capture-zscaler-client-connector) or Wireshark (if Zscaler Client Connector is not installed). You can then open the packet capture using Wireshark and type `tls.handshake.type==1` in the **Display**filter to view all the TLS handshakes containing the SNI extension.
  2. [Capture HTTP headers](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/how-capture-http-headers-har-file-client-system) and compare the **Host**value in the SNI or the domain in the Connect request with the Host header in the subsequent HTTP request.

### Solution

The following section describes the solution:

Zscaler doesn't recommend disabling the option **Block Domain Fronting** under **Administration**> **Advanced Settings** because it is a global setting applicable to the entire organization.

- If your business trusts a specific URL or Cloud App, you can choose to add it to the exemptions. See image.
- Alternatively, if your business trusts a specific application, you can choose to configure an SSL Inspection rule with the action **Do Not Inspect** for the concerned domain.

If none of the above steps help, submit a case to [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support) with the following information:

- If you have [enabled Remote Assistance](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/enabling-remote-assistance), complete URL and the timestamp when a user tried accessing it via Zscaler. Otherwise, Web Insights logs showing all the columns for the relevant transactions.
- HTTP header trace from the end user's system while accessing the concerned URL.
- Client packet capture (if [Zscaler Client Connector](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/enabling-packet-capture-zscaler-client-connector) is installed).

[Image: Domain Fronted SNI in a Web Insights log]

[Image: Domain Fronting]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->
