<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/troubleshooting-runbooks/inspected-despite-do-not-inspect-action","lastmod":"2026-07-29T15:30Z","nid":"1538871"} -->
## Inspected Despite a Do Not Inspect Action

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/inspected-despite-do-not-inspect-action
- Product: Zscaler Support Troubleshooting Runbooks
- Path: Zscaler Support Troubleshooting Runbooks > Internet & SaaS Access Control Policies Troubleshooting Runbook > SSL Inspection Issues > Inspected Despite a Do Not Inspect Action
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T15:30Z
- Summary: This article describes how to check why Internet & SaaS access policies inspected a URL despite a configured Do Not Inspect action.

This article describes how to check why Internet & SaaS (ZIA) access policies inspected a URL despite a configured Do Not Inspect action.

## How Is This Traffic Forwarded to Zscaler?

If the traffic from a known location is explicitly forwarded to Zscaler service on port 9443, the Service Edge always decrypts such traffic regardless of the SSL Inspection rules. To learn more, see [Deployment Scenarios for SSL Inspection](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/deployment-scenarios-ssl-inspection#Road-Warriors).

## How Is the SSL Inspection Rule Configured?

The following list helps determine how the SSL inspection rule is configured:

- Is **Show Notifications for Blocked Traffic** enabled in the rule?
- The Zscaler service must decrypt the transaction in order to display the End User Notification (EUN) in the user's browser. Generally in such cases, Zscaler service doesn't connect to the remote server because the policy decision based on the SSL handshake was to block the transaction.
- The Service Edge has access to more Layer 7 information in the web request due to this forced decryption, and then it might enforce an allow policy based on any additional criteria (if applicable). In that case, even though the Zscaler service initially decided to inspect the session only to show the EUN, the transaction is eventually allowed without displaying any EUN, or blocked if the transaction matches a more specific policy rule.

## Have You Enabled AI/ML-Based Content Categorization?

To determine if you have enabled AI/ML-based content categorization:

- If you have enabled this feature and configured SSL inspection for the Miscellaneous URL category, the Zscaler service initially inspects the transaction. However, the Service Edge can then determine a specific URL category based on the content in the server's response from content categorization that's based on artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning (ML).
- As a result, the Web logs can show that the category (e.g., Finance) URL transaction was inspected. But in this particular case, it was inspected because the URL was initially categorized as **Miscellaneous**.

## Does the URL Category Value in the Web Logs Match the Expected Category for this URL?

The following sections describe how to determine if the URL category value in the Web logs match the expected category for the URL.

- You don't need to create a custom category for every URL that must be allowed. For example, if you want to allow a URL that is logged as Professional Services, but it gets blocked with the reason `Not allowed to browse this category`, you need to first evaluate whether your business must block Professional Services for the given criteria.
- If your business requires blocking Professional Services for the concerned criteria, then you must create a Custom URL category that allows a set of one or more URLs while still blocking the parent category.

### No

For more information on how to proceed if the URLs don't match, see [How to Resolve User-Defined Category Conflicts](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/how-resolve-user-defined-category-conflicts).

### Yes

Ideally, the rule works as designed if the URL is correctly categorized. If you wish to choose a different action for this access using specific criteria, then create a rule above the applied rule with that action and more specific criteria.

## Does this Concern a Domain in the Miscellaneous URL Category?

The following sections describe what to do if a domain is in the miscellaneous URL category.

### Yes

1. Determine whether the domain is added under a user-defined **URL**category:
  - As soon as you add a URL to a user-defined **URL**category, it gets removed from the **Miscellaneous**category by design.
  - Note that the **Miscellaneous** category is a catch-all category for all the uncategorized URLs. In other words, for **Miscellaneous**or **Unknown**URLs, the behavior of **URLs retaining parent category**and **Keywords retaining parent category** is the same as **Custom URLs** and **Custom Keywords** respectively.
  - Solution: if you want a specific uncategorized domain to match the policy for Miscellaneous category, you must remove it from any custom categories. Else, you must define a similar policy rule for the user-defined category.
2. [Suspicious New Domains Lookup](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-advanced-policy-settings#DomainLookup) is enabled under **Advanced Policy Settings** for **URL & Cloud App Control**. If it is enabled, then any **Newly Registered** or **Observed Domain** is also classified under the **Miscellaneous**category.
3. Review the [URL's category in site review](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/using-site-review-lookup-urls). If the **Current Categories** column shows the value **Newly Registered and Observed Domains**, it means the domain in question was either recently registered or observed; in both these cases, Zscaler considers a domain suspicious for 30 days after its detection.
4. Note that even if **Miscellaneous**doesn't show as the category, all these domains are also treated as **Miscellaneous**because they aren't classified under a specific predefined category.
5. If you have different policy rules for the **Miscellaneous**,**Newly Registered**, and **Observed Domains** categories, then the rule at the top is enforced. Either ensure that both rules have the same action, or move the rule with the desired action just above the other rule. For example, if you want to block **Newly Registered**and **Observed Domains** categories, while allowing **Miscellaneous**, your block rule for the**Newly Registered** and **Observed Domains** category should be above the **Allow**rule for the **Miscellaneous**category.
6. If you have[enabled AI/ML based Content Categorization](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-advanced-policy-settings#Dynamic) under **Advanced Policy Settings** for **URL & Cloud App Control**, then policy enforcement for**SSL Inspected** transactions to a URL in the **Miscellaneous**category is deferred until Zscaler receives the response from the server.
7. If the server does not respond or if the client terminates the connection due to a timeout while the server has yet to provide a complete response, this may lead to policy not getting applied. In this case, the received bytes column should also show 0 in the web logs. There's no real issue here as the connection wasn't established between the client and the server because the client decided to terminate the connection. However, if a more consistent logging behavior is desired, you can disable AI/ML-based **Content Categorization**. Note that this is a global change.

If none of the above steps help, please submit a case to [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support) with the following information:

- If you have [enabled Remote Assistance](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/enabling-remote-assistance), the URL and the timestamp when a user tried accessing the web application via Zscaler. Otherwise, send Web Insights logs showing all the columns for the relevant transactions.
- Client packet capture (if [Zscaler Client Connector](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/enabling-packet-capture-zscaler-client-connector) is installed).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/troubleshooting-runbooks/internet-saas-access-control-policies-support-troubleshooting-runbook-0","lastmod":"2026-07-29T15:26Z","nid":"1539484"} -->
## Internet & SaaS Access Control Policies Support Troubleshooting Runbook

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/internet-saas-access-control-policies-support-troubleshooting-runbook-0
- Product: Zscaler Support Troubleshooting Runbooks
- Path: Zscaler Support Troubleshooting Runbooks > Internet & SaaS Access Control Policies Troubleshooting Runbook > Internet & SaaS Access Control Policies Support Troubleshooting Runbook
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T15:26Z
- Summary: This Zscaler runbook outlines troubleshooting steps for Internet & SaaS access control policies.

The Internet & SaaS Access Control Policies Support Troubleshooting Runbook provides comprehensive guidance for troubleshooting requests related to scenarios involving URL, domain, IP address, file analysis, and related vulnerabilities. It highlights various checks on third-party websites and Zscaler's tools that help you achieve clarity on the security verdicts. By following these structured steps, users can efficiently address issues related to Zscaler's access control policies and ensure proper handling of security threats.

## Triage

The following section describes the triage process for access control policies.

1. Does the website load after a delay or not at all?
  - **Delay or slowness**: Issues with [Internet & SaaS performance](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/zia-performance-troubleshooting-runbook).
  - **Other cases**: Continue.
2. Do transactions go through Zscaler?
  - **No or Not sure**: Traffic does not [go through Zscaler](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/zia-traffic-forwarding-troubleshooting-runbook).
  - **Other cases**: Continue.
3. Is the website using Quick UDP Internet Connections (QUIC)? Key benefits of QUIC include reduced latency due to faster connection establishment (0-RTT and 1-RTT handshakes), improved congestion control, and resilience to packet loss. It's widely used in http/3, where it enhances web performance by eliminating many inefficiencies associated with traditional TCP-based protocols.
  - **I don't know**: What is QUIC? QUIC, also known as http/3 or simply h3, is a transport protocol developed by Google that improves the performance of connection-oriented web applications. It operates over User Datagram Protocol (UDP) instead of TCP and integrates features like connection migration, multiplexing without head-of-line blocking, and built-in encryption (TLS 1.3).

To learn more, see [Managing the QUIC Protocol](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/managing-quic-protocol).

To determine if a website is using QUIC, see [How to Determine if a Website is Using QUIC](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/how-determine-if-website-using-quic).

## More Troubleshooting Options

These issues can be broadly classified into the three categories, described in the following sections. Follow the symptoms that are the closest match to your case.

Assistance With Policy Configuration

If you want to know if your policy configuration is correct or if a resource is correctly categorized by Zscaler.

- **URL Filtering**: [Resolve user-defined URL category conflicts](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/how-resolve-user-defined-category-conflicts).
- **SSL Inspection**: [Add Zscaler's certificate](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/adding-custom-certificate-application-specific-trust-store) to a specific application's certificate store.
- **Cloud App**: [Cloud app instance](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/adding-cloud-application-instance), [tenant profile / tenancy restriction](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/adding-tenant-profiles).
- **URL Filtering / Cloud App**: Look up the [URL Category and Cloud App](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/using-site-review-lookup-urls) for a given URL.

Policy Not Working as Expected

The policy is correctly configured but the web or firewall logs show a contradicting policy action.

- The Allow policy is configured but access gets blocked or cautioned as confirmed by the web logs. Look at the **Policy Action** field's value for the concerned URL and click one of the following:
  - [Undecryptable Traffic Block](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/undecryptable-traffic-block)
  - [Not Allowed to Use HTTP Tunnel](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/not-allowed-use-http-tunnel)
  - [Blocked Due to Server Probe Failure](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/blocked-due-server-probe-failure)
  - [Access Denied Due to Bad Server Certificate](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/access-denied-due-bad-server-certificate)
  - [Blocked Due to Bad SSL Record](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/blocked-due-bad-ssl-record)
  - [Access Denied Due to Domain Fronting](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/access-denied-due-domain-fronting)
  - [Not Allowed to Browse this Category](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/not-allowed-browse-category)
  - **Other reasons**: Submit a case to [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support) containing the information mentioned in Initial Information Set.
- **SSL Inspection**: There are no exemptions in SSL Inspection policy but traffic does not get inspected as confirmed by the web logs. Look at the **SSL Policy Reason** field's value for the concerned URL and refer to the [SSL Policy Reason Runbook](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/ssl-policy-reason-runbook).
- **SSL Inspection**: [Untrusted Server Certificate Gets Allowed](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/untrusted-server-certificate-gets-allowed)
- **SSL Inspection**: [Inspected Despite Do Not Inspect Action in the Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/inspected-despite-do-not-inspect-action)
- **Cloud App**: [Block Action is Configured for One Activity but All Activities Get Allowed as Confirmed by the Web Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/cloud-app-block-action-configured-one-activity-all-activities-get-allowed-confirmed-web-logs)
- **Firewall Control**:
  - [Allow Due to Insufficient App Data](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/allow-due-insufficient-app-data)
  - [Bypassed Due to Missing Config](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/bypassed-due-missing-config)
- [Specific Criteria in the Access Control Policy are not Correctly Matching the Transactions](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/specific-criteria-access-control-policy-do-not-match)
- Other issues where the web logs confirm that the policy is not working as expected: Submit a case to [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support) containing the information mentioned in Initial Information Set.

Other General Access Issues

None of the earlier options apply to your case.

- [Unable to Access Specific Websites or Web Applications](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/unable-access-specific-websites-or-applications)
- [Block Policy Configured but Access Gets Allowed](https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/block-policy-configured-access-gets-allowed)

## Initial Information Set

[Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support) recommends that you enable Remote Assistance in view-only mode. Additionally, provide the following information:

- Client IP from the impacted end user's system (output of `ipconfig /all` and `route print 165.225.*` from a command prompt on a Windows PC and output of `ifconfig /all` and `route get 165.225.0.0` from a terminal on a Mac system).
- A screenshot of the complete page at [https://ip.zscaler.com](https://ip.zscaler.com).
- A screenshot of the error message seen in the web browser or the application, if applicable.
- The timestamp or period during which this access was attempted.
- Complete URL or Destination IP of the application.
- Policy Name or a screenshot of the relevant policy.

Alternatively, if remote assistance cannot be enabled, download the Web Insights logs containing all the columns for the corresponding period. It's best to use not more than 2–3 relevant filters to optimize the number of logs in the exported file while still retaining a wide enough context for analysis. Some useful filters: URL Search, User, Client IP, Location.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/troubleshooting-runbooks/internet-saas-dlp-policies-support-troubleshooting-runbook","lastmod":"2026-08-07T21:06Z","nid":"1532308"} -->
## Internet & SaaS DLP Policies Support Troubleshooting Runbook

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/troubleshooting-runbooks/internet-saas-dlp-policies-support-troubleshooting-runbook
- Product: Zscaler Support Troubleshooting Runbooks
- Path: Zscaler Support Troubleshooting Runbooks > Internet & SaaS DLP Policies Support Troubleshooting Runbook
- Last modified: 2026-08-07T21:06Z
- Summary: This Zscaler runbook outlines troubleshooting steps for Internet & SaaS Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies.

The Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Policies Support Troubleshooting Runbook serves as a comprehensive guide for configuring, fine-tuning, and troubleshooting Zscaler's DLP solutions across various scopes. It provides step-by-step methodologies to address common challenges encountered during DLP deployment and operation. The troubleshooting framework outlined in the runbook emphasizes a systematic approach by leveraging internal tools such as Web Insights logs and detailed configuration checks. By adhering to these systematic troubleshooting steps, the DLP Policy Runbook enables organizations to enhance the accuracy, effectiveness, and resilience of their data protection strategies.

## Require DLP Feature Configuration Assistance or DLP Policy Fine-Tuning

Zscaler DLP offers various enhancement features that are enabled on-demand or require an additional subscription. The following examples are a few enhancements DLP policies provide.

- [Support for Correlated View of App Users and DLP File Access](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/release-upgrade-summary-2025?applicable_category=zscaler.net&deployment_date=2025-05-16&id=1525346): To view the information on the Files tab, you must have a license for SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP, and you must configure the DLP scan. To upgrade your license, contact your Zscaler Account team.
- [Support for SaaS Security API Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy Rules without Content Inspection](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/release-upgrade-summary-2025): To enable this feature for your organization, contact [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support).
- [New Predefined DLP Engines](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/release-upgrade-summary-2025): These engines are available by default for users with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. For enablement on existing tenants, contact [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support).

Look for the following information in the [Zscaler’s Help Portal](https://help.zscaler.com/zia) or [Release Notes](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/release-notes):

- Contact your Zscaler Account team: The feature might require an additional subscription or an additional SKU, depending on your current Zscaler’s subscription. Contact your Zscaler Account team for more information.
- Contact [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support): The feature is not enabled automatically for all users. Raise a Provisioning support case with Zscaler Support with the feature details and reference link from Zscaler’s Help Portal or Release Notes.

If users have configured the DLP policy but want to fine-tune the policy, consider the following policy option, if applicable:

1. Configure the **Minimum Data Size (KB)**. Zscaler DLP engines support files up to 400 MB and can scan the first 100 MB of the extracted text. The maximum size also applies to files extracted from archive files. If files exceed defined thresholds for size or format compatibility, DLP inspection could fail or skip triggering policies for those files.

Review the DLP false positive events to determine a feasible value for **Minimum Data Size (KB)**. For example, if there is a lot of telemetry data smaller than 10 KB that contributes to a large volume of false positives, you can configure the **Minimum Data Size (KB)** as 10 KB and monitor again.

1. Create a **DLP Allowlist** rule for HTTP Form Data based on the **Custom Allowlist URL** category. This category includes file type fallback decisions by Zscaler.
  - For single-part non-URL-encoded requests, the default is **HTTP non-file text data**.
  - For multipart requests and single-part URL-encoded requests, the default is **HTTP Form data**.
2. Avoid configuring a catch-all DLP policy rule with ANY file type. Due to the file type fallback decisions by Zscaler, you can drop HTTP Form data from the file type list of the last catch-all rule.
3. Use a combination of a **Predefined Dictionary** with a **Low**or **Medium Confidence Score Threshold**and a **Custom Dictionary** for **Pattern/Phrase**.

For example, you can create a Custom Dictionary to include keywords using patterns and phrases:

See image.

- Leverage the Predefined dictionary **NRIC Numbers (Singapore)**.
- Create a new DLP Engine by using the Predefined dictionary **NRIC Numbers (Singapore) and Custom Dictionary**.

Use the Expression Preview: ((NRIC Numbers (Singapore) > 5) AND ((Identity Card Number (Phrases 1) > 0) OR (Identity Card Number (Phrases 2) > 0)))

See image.

## Web DLP Policy (Inline DLP, OCR, EDM, and IDM) Not Working as Expected

When handling DLP policy issues, look at two areas: the DLP policy configuration on Zscaler and the input data.

The DLP policy is configured to match the DLP Engine or other criteria (with or without content matching), but the access is not triggered. You must look at the Web Insights logs for the **Blocked Policy Type** value and the **Allowed DLP Rule Name** for the reported transaction.

By default, the Zscaler service evaluates inline DLP policy rules according to rule order, with the evaluation stopping at the first match. However, if [Evaluate All Rules mode](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-dlp-policy-rules-evaluate-all-rules-mode) is enabled for your organization, you can instead have the Zscaler service evaluate all rules, and enforce the rule with the most restrictive action. [Evaluate All Rules mode](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-dlp-policy-rules-evaluate-all-rules-mode) uses rule order only when multiple rules with the same action are matched. In that case, the rule order determines which policy rule is triggered.

Sample Web Insights Logs

The following are important Web insights fields for DLP issues.

Keep in mind that policy action depends on the [Evaluate All Rules mode](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-dlp-policy-rules-evaluate-all-rules-mode) setting:

See image.

- By Rule Order: Zscaler service evaluates inline DLP policy rules according to rule order, with evaluation stopping at the first match.
- Evaluate All Rules: Zscaler service evaluates all rules, enforcing the rules with the most restrictive action. Evaluate All Rules mode uses rule order only when multiple rules with the same action are matched. In that case, the rule order determines which policy rule is triggered.

| URL | DLP Engine | DLP Dictionaries | Blocked Policy Name | Blocked Policy Type | Allowed DLP Rule Name |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dlptest.com/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php | SSN | SSN Regex 2 (4) | DLP_Block_SSN | Data Loss Prevention | DLP_Pre724_otherDoc |
| dlptest.com/http-post/ | Hash Engine | test (2) | DLP_Rule_Phrase | Data Loss Prevention | DLP_Pre724_otherDoc |
| lastpass.com/login_check.php | External | None | None | None | DLP_Pre724_otherDoc |
| lastpass.com/login_check.php | External | None | None | None | DLP_Pre724_otherDoc |
| storage.prod.us-east-1.w1.dataprotection.zscalergov.net/browser-extensions/ | External | None | DLP_Password | Data Loss Prevention | None |
| endpoints.prod.us-east-1.w1.dataprotection.zscalergov.net/api/ | 26-Thailand National Identity Card Number | 26-Thailand National Identity Card Number (Patterns) (1);26-Thailand National Identity Card Number (Phrases) (1) | DLP_NRIC_SEA | Data Loss Prevention | None |

Troubleshooting

If the**Blocked Policy Type** and **Allowed DLP Rule Name** isn't **None**, this means the request matched the DLP policy. Check the following in the full web insights logs and Internet & SaaS configuration:

1. Ensure the reported traffic is seen on the Web Insights logs. If the web transaction is not visible in the Internet & SaaS Web Insights logs, it is possible that the transaction is not reaching Zscaler.
2. Ensure SSL inspection is enabled if the traffic is HTTPS.
3. Go to **Policies**>**Data Protection**>**Common Resources**>**Advanced Settings** and verify the following configuration:
  1. Check that the request traffic is included in any of the **Cloud App & URL Exceptions for DLP** configuration. These configurations are a global setting. Do not change them without fully understanding the change and impact.
    - **Exempted Cloud Applications**: Add the respective cloud app if you want to bypass DLP policy.
    - **Exempted URLs**: Add the respective domains if you want to bypass DLP policy.
    - **Exempted User-Defined URL Categories**: Add the respective **Custom URL** category if you want to bypass DLP policy.
    - **Exempt URL Encoded Data**: Enable this setting to bypass scanning the content type as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` from DLP evaluation.
  2. Go to **Exact Data Match**> **Check for Popular Formats:** Enabling this reduces false positives on non-standard formats. Exact Data Match (EDM) and Indexed Document Match (IDM) require the Advanced DLP suite.
  3. Go to **Optical Character Recognition (OCR)**: Enable these settings if you want to apply DLP policy on image files.
4. Review and take notes on the specific triggered DLP rule (in the Web Insights **Blocked Policy Type** or **Allowed DLP Rule Name**).
  1. Check if the transaction matches all the criteria configured within a DLP rule:
    - **Source-related criteria**: These include Users, Groups, Departments, User Risk Profile, Locations, Location Groups, Source IP Groups.
    - **Destination-related criteria**: These include URL Categories, Cloud Applications, Cloud Application Instances, Private Access Application Segment. The DLP policy applies AND logic to the URL Categories and Cloud Applications fields when inspecting your organization's traffic. In order for a DLP rule to trigger, the Zscaler service must detect the rule’s selected URL categories and cloud applications in a transaction.
    - **Other criteria**: This includes Time, Protocols, File Type, and Data Size (KB). Notes: [WebSocket Protocol](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/release-upgrade-summary-2025?applicable_category=zscaler.net&deployment_date=2025-05-09&id=1524391) is now supported in DLP rule.
  2. If **Content Matching** is enabled, record which DLP Engines are selected. Based on the DLP Engines in use, go to **Administration** > **Resources** > **Data Loss Prevention** > **DLP Dictionaries & Engines** to learn more details:
    1. First, check the respective DLP Engines to learn which DLP Dictionaries are involved and their **Expression**.
    2. View the respective DLP Engine and take a screenshot or record the **Expression Preview.** See image.
    3. When you know the DLP Dictionaries used, view the respective **DLP Dictionary** and take a screenshot. See image.
    4. Check the settings and values configured in each related DLP Dictionary:
      - **Predefined Type**: Note the **Confidence Score Threshold**and **Proximity Length**.
      - Special configurations like **Custom High Confidence Phrases** and **Social Security Numbers** in **Social Security Numbers (US)**.
      - **Patterns & Phrases**
      - **EDM**
      - **IDM**

1. If you have the DLP violation alert, cross-check the DLP violation criteria with the earlier steps. If your current DLP Notification Template does not include `"${DLPTRIGGERS}"`, you can create a new DLP Notification Template using the following example: See image.

If your current DLP Notification Template does not include `"${DLPTRIGGERS}"`. You can create a new DLP Notification Template using the following example in the **Message as HTML** section.

```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
<style>
.user {color: rgb(1, 81, 152);}
.url {color: rgb(1, 81, 152);}
.postingtype {color: rgb(1, 81, 152);}
.engines {color: rgb(1, 81, 152);}
.dictionaries {color: rgb(1, 81, 152);}
</style>
</head>
<body>
The attached content triggered a Web DLP rule for your organization.
<br/><br/>
Transaction Timestamp: <span class="timestamp">${TIMESTAMP}</span>
<br/>
Transaction ID: <span class="transaction_id">${TRANSACTION_ID}</span>
<br/>
Client IP Accessing the URL: <span class="client_ip">${CLIENT_IP}</span>
<br/>
User Accessing the URL: <span class="user">${USER}</span>
<br/>
Action for the access: <span class="action">${ACTION}</span>
<br/>
Rulename of DLP policy: <span class="rulename">${RULENAME}</span>
<br/>
Severity of Violation: <span class="severity">${SEVERITY}</span>
<br/>
URL Accessed: <span class="url">${URL}</span>
<br/>
Posting Type: <span class="postingtype">${TYPE}</span>
<br/>
DLP MD5: <span class="dlpmd5">${DLPMD5}</span>
<br/>
File Name: <span class="filename">${FILENAME}</span>
<br/>
File Type: <span class="filetype">${FILETYPE}</span>
<br/>
Triggered DLP Violation Engines (assigned to the hit rule): <span class="engines">${ENGINES_IN_RULE}</span>
<br/>
Triggered DLP Violation Dictionaries (assigned to the hit rule): <span class="dictionaries">${DICTIONARIES}</span>
<br/><br/>
DLP Triggers match: <span class="triggers">${DLPTRIGGERS}</span>
<br/>
No action is required on your part.
<br/><br/>
</body>
</html>
```

1. If no issue is found in the DLP Engines or DLP Dictionaries, check if the content is **POST**using single or multipart form submission. There is a possibility that part of a multipart/form-data payload submission hits the DLP rule.

#### How to Check Multipart Form Submission

A user can submit a POST request to Zscaler using a single or multipart payload submission. This affects the way the Zscaler’s DLP engine processes the data.

For example, when a user selects a single file or multiple files in one single upload, one or more files are uploaded to a website like http://dlptest.com/http-post/ using the multipart/form-data option. In a multipart payload upload, the data is divided into multiple parts with its own headers and boundaries. Each of the parts is evaluated against the Zscaler's DLP rules.

The following Chrome Browser Header indicates a multipart payload upload.

See image.

Further Consideration

At this point, you should have verified most of the DLP-related configuration on the Zscaler Admin Console and nothing is out of the norm. You might have to create an issue summary with the compiled data and open a support case with [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support).

Here is a quick checklist of the data collection:

1. HTTP Header HAR file
  - [Capturing HTTP Headers on Microsoft Edge](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/capturing-http-headers-microsoft-edge).
  - [Capturing HTTP Headers on Google Chrome](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/capturing-http-headers-google-chrome).
  - [Capturing HTTP Headers on Mozilla Firefox](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/capturing-http-headers-mozilla-firefox).
  - [Capturing HTTP Headers on Safari](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/capturing-http-headers-safari).
2. Wireshark capture
  - For Zscaler Client Connector, use the [Packet Capture option](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/enabling-packet-capture-zscaler-client-connector).
  - Without Zscaler Client Connector, use the [Wireshark capture method](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsug_html_chunked/ChapterCapture.html).
3. Web Insights logs with all fields selected.
4. Violation content notification email or JSON file.

You can remove or obfuscate the highly sensitive data while it is still able to trigger the DLP issue.

1. Sample test data. (You can skip this if the same data was provided earlier.)
2. Temporarily enable [Remote Assistance](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/enabling-remote-assistance).

## Web DLP Email or ICAP Notification Issue

Zscaler supports sending DLP violation notification delivery using email, Internet Content Adaptation Protocol (ICAP). You can integrate the ICAP option (subscription required) with a third-party ICAP server or Zscaler Incident. To learn more, see [ICAP server](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-icap-communication-between-zscaler-and-dlp-servers) or [Zscaler Incident Receiver](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/policies/data-loss-prevention/dlp-incident-receiver).

### Troubleshooting

The following sections describe troubleshooting for web DLP.

Email Notification Issue

For Email Notification:

1. Zscaler supports a 25 MB limit for DLP email notification attachments by default. The admin still receives the DLP email notification but without the violation content attachment. The DLP email shows a message like this:

```
Posting Type: General Browsing Post (NRIC-Large.xlsx not attached - its size 51530124 bytes exceeds archive size limit of 25MB)
```

See image.

##### Further Steps

- What is the use case and investigate why you want to send large violation content using email.
- Use other options such as leveraging the ICAP method (integration with a third-party ICAP server, Zscaler Incident Receiver, or Zscaler Workflow Automation).
- If you have a strong, valid use case to send large violation content using email, then raise a Provisioning support case with [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support) with the details.

SMTP Delivery Issue

If the DLP policy is triggered as per Zscaler logs, and you are not getting email notifications to the configured auditor email address, then use the following sections.

##### SMTP Codes Reference

Zscaler Support can check the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) code for a particular email delivery using the DLP Identifier field from Web Insights logs. SMTP codes are three-digit numbers, such as 250, 421, or 550. The first digit indicates the general category of the response:

- 2.x.x: Positive completion reply (success).
- 3.x.x: Positive intermediate reply (command accepted, more information needed).
- 4.x.x: Transient negative completion reply (temporary error).
- 5.x.x: Permanent negative completion reply (permanent error).

Common examples:

- 220: Service ready (SMTP server is ready to accept connections).
- 250: Requested mail action okay (message delivered successfully).
- 421: Service not available, closing transmission channel (temporary issue with the server).
- 450: Requested mail action not taken: mailbox unavailable (temporary issue with the recipient's mailbox).
- 451: Requested action aborted: local error in processing (temporary error on the server).
- 500: Syntax error, command unrecognized (invalid command).
- 550: Requested action not taken: mailbox unavailable or not found (permanent error).
- 554: Transaction failed (general error during message transmission).

##### Troubleshooting

1. Check the auditor's email address. From the Zscaler Admin Console, find the external auditor's email address by editing the relevant DLP rule. Ensure the auditor email address is correct. You can test it using a different email address (with a different email domain (e.g., gmail.com or yahoo.com).

See image.

This step is not a workaround or solution but a problem isolation step. Since DLP violation might involve sensitive data, you must get the necessary internal approval before performing this test.

1. Check the Web Insights logs. You can filter the Web Insights logs to display the DLP transactions. Look for the **Policy Action** column, ensure the notification for DLP was triggered as either **Violates Compliance Category, archived to mailbox**, or **Allowed and archived to mailbox**.

##### Further Steps

At this point, you can compile the issue summary with the data and open a support case with [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support). Here is a quick checklist of the data collection:

1. Relevant configuration screenshots:
  1. DLP rule name
  2. Auditor email address
2. Web Insights logs with all fields selected.
3. Temporarily enable **Remote Assistance**. To learn more, see [Enabling Remote Assistance](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/enabling-remote-assistance).

ICAP Notification Issue

Zscaler supports secure or unencrypted ICAP receivers on the DLP notification. Zscaler recommends sending transaction information via secure ICAP.

Secure ICAP is required to set up stunnel application.

To learn more, see [About ICAP Communication Between Zscaler and DLP Servers](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-icap-communication-between-zscaler-and-dlp-servers).

See image.

##### Troubleshooting

1. Ensure the necessary Firewall configuration according to Zscaler's Config page.
  - **DLP ICAP Requirements**. Use the following URL format: `https://config.zscaler.com/``<zscaler cloud>``/icap`, where you should replace <zscaler cloud> with your Zscaler cloud URL (e.g., https://config.zscaler.com/zscaler.net/icap).
  - **DLP Incident Receiver**. Use the following URL format: `https://config.zscaler.com/``<zscaler cloud>``/dlp-incident-receiver`, where you should replace <zscaler cloud> with your Zscaler cloud URL (e.g., https://config.zscaler.com/zscaler.net/dlp-incident-receiver).
  - **Internet & SaaS Advanced DLP (Private Service Edge)**. Use the following URL format: `https://config.zscaler.com/``<zscaler cloud>``/zia-private-dlp`, where you should replace <zscaler cloud> with your Zscaler cloud URL (e.g., https://config.zscaler.com/zscaler.net/zia-private-dlp).
  - **Private Service Edge for Internet & SaaS Access Requirements**. Use the following URL format: `https://config.zscaler.com/``<zscaler cloud>``/zia-sedge`, where you should replace <zscaler cloud> with your Zscaler cloud URL (e.g., https://config.zscaler.com/zscaler.net/zia-sedge).
2. Perform a telnet to the external ICAP server IP address and port (e.g., 1344) behind an allowed network.
3. If it is ICAP, check the stunnel configuration according to the tunnel application guide. Change the configuration to an unencrypted ICAP URL and test again.

##### Further Steps

At this point, you can compile the issue summary with the data and open a support case with [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/contact-support). Here is a quick checklist of the data collection:

- Relevant configuration screenshots:
  - DLP rule name
  - DLP rule’s DLP Incident Receiver setting
  - DLP Incident Receiver’s configuration
- Web Insights logs with all fields selected.
- Temporarily enable **Remote Assistance**. To learn more, see [Enabling Remote Assistance](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/enabling-remote-assistance).

- Summary: The Internet & SaaS File Type Control Policy Support Troubleshooting Runbook provides step-by-step troubleshooting instructions for resolving common File Type Control issues encountered in Internet & SaaS.

The Internet & SaaS File Type Control Policy Support Troubleshooting Runbook provides step-by-step troubleshooting instructions for resolving common File Type Control issues encountered in Internet & SaaS.

## Understanding How File Type Control Detection Works

Zscaler’s File Type Control policy enables administrators to create filtering rules to restrict the upload or download of specific file types, including unknown or unrecognized ones.

To ensure efficient and accurate enforcement of these rules, Zscaler leverages file signatures, MIME types, and extensions to detect a file’s true type. This helps Zscaler validate files beyond just their extensions.

To learn more, see the following articles:

- [About File Type Control](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-file-type-control) for additional information on File Type Control policies.
- [Understanding Policy Enforcement](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-policy-enforcement) for details on how File Type Control policies fit into the broader Zscaler policy enforcement workflow.

## Validate if the Issue is Related to File Type Control Policy

Before troubleshooting a reported issue, it is essential to confirm whether File Type Control is responsible for the block or unexpected behavior. Various security policies, such as Malware Protection, Sandbox, Cloud App Control, or other upstream security solutions, can also impact file upload/download. To ensure accurate troubleshooting, first verify the logs and user experience to determine if the issue is indeed related to File Type Control.

End User Notification

Validate if the issue or block is related to File Type Control by reviewing the End User Notification.

See image.

Web Insights Log

You can also validate from the Web Insights Logs if the block is related to File Type Control. The following are the Web Insights Logs related to File Type Control:

| Policy Action | Download File Type | Download File Name | Blocked Policy Type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| File Type download cautioned File Type upload cautioned File Type upload/download cautioned | <File Type Cautioned> | <Cautioned Filename> | File Type Control |
| Not allowed to access this file type Not allowed to upload/download files of this type | <File Type Blocked> | <Blocked Filename> | File Type Control |

## Policy Behavior Issues

Users can report cases where files are incorrectly blocked or files are not correctly identified. These issues can arise due to policy misconfigurations or forwarding errors. The following sections outline common policy-related issues and steps to resolve them.

Files Not Allowed or Blocked as Per the Policy

Users can report that a specific File Type Control policy is not applied correctly (e.g., download/upload is not blocked as expected).

#### Validate SSL Inspection

File Type Control policies require SSL Inspection to function properly.

##### Check Web Insights Logs

To check the Web Insights Logs:

1. Filter logs for the affected domain and inspect the **SSL Policy Reason**column. See image.
2. Confirm that the policies in the **Policy Reason**column are inspected. See image.
3. If **SSL Policy Reason** is **Bypassed**:
  - Review your SSL Inspection policies.
  - Update the policies as needed to ensure SSL Inspection is applied appropriately.

#### Verify Supported Protocols

To verify supported protocols:

1. Ensure the protocol involved in the transaction is supported by File Type Control policies. The supported protocols are:
  - HTTP
  - HTTPS
  - FTP over HTTP
  - Native FTP
2. Filter Web Insights Logs and review the **Protocol**column.
3. If the protocol is unsupported, File Type Control policies are not applicable.

#### Confirm Rule Match Conditions

If the File Type Control policy relies on specific attributes (e.g., URL Category, Cloud App, User, Location), ensure these conditions match.

- Filter Web Insights Logs for the affected domain.
- Review these key fields and any other fields configured as the policy criteria:
  - URL Category
  - Cloud App
  - User
  - Location
- Adjust the policy if the conditions do not align. Test the updated policy behavior.

#### Review Criteria for Active Content or Unscannable Files

- **Active Content**: Only applies to Microsoft Office and PDF files.
- **Unscannable Files**: Refers to files Zscaler cannot scan.
- Check the Web Insights logs for the **Unscannable Type** entry. If **None**is logged, the file was successfully scanned. In this case, rules targeting **Unscannable Files** do not apply.
- Temporarily deselect the **Active Content** or **Unscannable Files** criteria in the policy to identify if these settings are causing the issue. See image.

Archive File Policy Mismatch

When users report issues such as archive files (e.g., ZIP) are blocked despite having an allow policy, the contents in the archive might trigger policy rules. Zscaler uses deep packet inspection to analyze files inside archives. If a blocked file type (e.g., an image file) exists within the archive, the entire archive is blocked.

For instance, if your goal is to block image files while allowing archive files, you would first configure a policy to block image files, followed by an allow rule for archive files, as demonstrated in the following image.

See image.

In this case, if the ZIP file contains blocked file types (e.g., images), the upload/download of the archive file is blocked by the image file rule. This is confirmed by using the Web Insights Logs under the **Blocked Policy Name** field.

See image.

This is expected behavior because Zscaler uses deep packet inspection to scan and apply policies to individual files inside the archive. Any priority rule blocking access to the actual file inside Archive blocks the connection.

Ensure rules blocking the specific inner file types are deprioritized after the allow rule for archives.

Allowed Files Blocked as *Not Allowed to Upload/Download Unscannable File Formats*

Even if a file type (e.g., .bz2) is allowed by an File Type Control policy, users can encounter a block message stating `Not allowed to upload/download unscannable file formats`.

See image.

Zscaler **Malware Protection** > **Unscannable Files Block** settings take precedence over File Type Control policies. If the **Malware Protection** setting is configured to block unscannable files, it overrides File Type Control allow rules.

#### Explain Unscannable Files in Malware Protection Policy

- Applies to upload or download files that the Zscaler service is unable to scan.
- Unscannable files are files that Zscaler cannot scan due to:
  - Unrecognized file format: Malformed, truncated, or encrypted files.
  - Excessive file size: Files (e.g., Microsoft Office documents) exceeding specific size limits, such as 400 MB.
  - Excessive compression: Files compressed or archived more than 5 times.

- Review the Web Insights Logs to confirm **Blocked Policy Type** as **Malware Protection**. See image.

- Verify that the error message matches the description.
- Create a security exception for the relevant URLs:
  - Go to **Policies** >**Cybersecurity**> **Malware Protection**> **Security Exceptions**.
  - Add the specific URLs under **Do Not Scan Content from these URLs**. See image.
- Test and confirm that the file is uploaded or downloaded.

File Type is Incorrectly Identified

There are instances where files are blocked because their file type is misidentified. For example, a Dynamic Link Library (.dll) file might be detected as an .exe file, resulting in a block if .exe files are restricted.

See image.

As in this example, the website is utilizing a .dll extension that Zscaler identifies as an .exe file. If the organization's policy restricts .exe files, the upload/download is blocked, causing the reported issue.

See image.

This issue can occur because Zscaler does not solely rely on file extensions to identify file types. Instead, it validates the true file type by analyzing the file signature, which represent the file’s actual structure.

Discrepancies can occur due to:

- **Mismatch Between File Extension and True File Type**: The file extension was renamed manually without altering the file’s contents.
- **Corrupted or Incomplete Files**: The file could have been partially overwritten, leading to incorrect magic bytes.
- **Website-Specific Behaviors**: Some websites can use non-standard file naming conventions or mechanisms.

Validate the file’s true type by analyzing its file signature.

#### How to Analyze the True File Type

To identify the true file type of a file, you can analyze its hex signature on a Linux OS. You can use a file utility to confirm the true file type of a file.

```
mmir@PF3QYHZJ:~$ file image.png
    image.png: PNG image data, 800 x 600, 8-bit/color RGBA, non-interlaced
```

```
mmir@PF3QYHZJ:~$ file GT.CIP.IRG.Client.dll
GT.CIP.IRG.Client.dll: PE32 executable (console) Intel 80386 Mono/.Net assembly, for MS Windows
```

Compare the identified file type with the policy rules. If the true type is blocked due to policy restrictions:

- Modify the File Type Control policy specific to this domain or file type, if appropriate.
- Contact the destination vendor for clarification and identifying the mismatch between the file signature and file extension.
